Did you ever stop your prescribed medicines course once your symptoms disappeared? Or have you taken tablets when you didn’t need them?

Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials can drive #AntimicrobialResistance (#AMR), in which bacteria evolve to survive these medicines.

And the cost of inaction is enormous. The WHO estimates that treating resistant bacterial #infections alone could cost the world USD 412 billion every year by 2035.

At C-CAMP, we are working with national and international partners to tackle AMR.

We’re excited to launch the 7th edition of C-CAMP @CARB_X 𝐀𝐌𝐑 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔, supporting breakthrough R&D and innovation to address antimicrobial resistance.

AMR innovators from any domain — #Diagnostics, Non-traditional #therapeutics, #Preventatives, and Direct-Acting Small Molecules — can apply.

Check out the Focus Areas and Offerings in the attached poster.

Day 3 | Partnerships, Fundraising Readiness & Founder Evolution

The final day of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program focused on building long-term scale engines - partnerships, investor readiness, and leadership evolution.

We began with “Channel & Partnerships: Designing a Partner Engine That Scales,” led by Venkat Shyam. Founders explored how structured channel #strategies, aligned incentives, and ecosystem #collaborations can unlock non-linear growth beyond direct sales.

In the #Fundraising Deep Dive: #Investor-Grade Company — From Pitch to Process & Metrics That Raise Money, Ravindra Krishnappa emphasized building companies that are investment-ready by design. The session broke down traction KPIs, investors' trust, #governance discipline, narrative clarity, and process maturity.

The program concluded with “Org & Leadership for Scaling: Founder-to-CEO Transition” led by Sathyanarayana B V, followed by final reflections and key takeaways. The conversation centered on building leadership depth, creating accountable org structures, and evolving from operator to strategic decision-maker. Sathyanarayana B V also spoke about #HR Management Grid, Leadership styles, how each one of them affects and has an impact in different workplaces, and how leaders are born or lost under different #leadership style

Scaling a startup ultimately requires more than #strategy - it demands founder transformation.

We thank all our expert #mentors and participating #founders for making this acceleration journey deeply insightful and impact-driven. At DERBI Foundation, our commitment remains clear: enabling startups with the right #ecosystem, right #frameworks, and right #mentorship to scale sustainably.

Dayananda Sagar University- DSU | Dr.Premachandra Sagar | Rohan Prem Sagar | Sathyanarayana B V | Bhavani G | Sowmya Sathish | Santhiya S | Adithya K

#DERBIFoundation #StartupScaling #FundraisingReadiness #Leadership #Partnerships #AccelerationProgram #Innovation

Day 2 | Expanding Markets, Strengthening Financial Foundations

Day 2 of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program shifted the lens from internal readiness to external expansion and financial resilience.

The day opened with “Market Access Strategy: #IndiaExpansion + Global Entry Readiness” led by Shivi Jain. Startups explored structured approaches to entering new markets, from regulatory preparedness and localization strategy to channel partnerships and #global positioning. The focus was on building scalable access, not opportunistic expansion.

In the Cashflow & Working Capital War-Room: Scale Without Dying, Nayak guided founders through one of the most underestimated growth levers — liquidity discipline. Through real-world scenarios and financial stress-testing frameworks, startups examined burn cycles, receivables management, and #capital efficiency as core survival metrics.

The day concluded with “Deal Structuring & Term Sheet Masterclass: Don’t Lose the Company” by Sharath Shyamasunder, The Startup Zone, where founders unpacked #investor clauses, dilution mechanics, control rights, and long-term implications of #fundraising decisions.

Growth is exciting. But #sustainable scale is built on informed expansion, disciplined capital management, and smart deal-making.

Up to 15% of food produced in India perishes due to lack of refrigeration. Medicines and vaccines also depend on consistent cooling from storage to delivery. Yet refrigeration remains unaffordable to many farmers and traders due to high upfront costs. Reefer trucks running on fossil fuels add to the ecological cost of this operation as well. Currently, there exists a gap of 3.2+ million metric tonne in India’s cold-chain capacity. 

Tan90 Thermal, one of the winners of Social Alpha’s Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy (Edition 3), has developed a low-cost, proprietary Phase Change Material-based portable cold storage solution, offered as cooling-as-a-service, to make farm-to-fork transportation more efficient and less carbon-intensive. 
Tan90 Thermal is an example of how hands-on mentorship, product development assistance, and catalytic funding can reimagine innovation in energy access and efficiency, especially in critical sectors like food and pharma. 

If your innovation can make a real impact on energy access, efficiency, storage, or the transition to renewables, apply to Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy.

This is exactly the kind of bottleneck we are looking to solve. 

Rechargion Energy was one of the winners of Social Alpha’s Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy (Edition 3), receiving product development support, mentorship, and a mix of dilutive and non-dilutive funding aiding its growth.
The result? A leap from early-stage prototype (TRL 3) to a field-ready, validated technology (TRL 7).

We're looking for more innovators building in this space, including alternate battery chemistries, long-duration storage, and resource-efficient storage technologies that can strengthen India's energy future.

iCreate IGNITE+ 2.0 brings together incubators, ecosystem leaders and innovation enablers to exchange ideas, share experiences and explore how we can build stronger startup ecosystems.

The day began with a warm welcome and an insightful address by Dr.Praveen D., Head - TBI, iCreate, who introduced the iCreate ecosystem and the vision behind IGNITE+ 2.0.

We then heard from Mr Dharmesh Parmar, Joint Commissioner of Industries, Government of Gujarat, on government support and the journey of startups towards becoming scalable SMEs and beyond. Dr. Yogesh Patil, Former Co-Founder of Biosense Technologies, shared valuable lessons from the HealthTech and MedTech journey, including the realities of building products and finding product-market fit.

The morning wrapped up with a candid roundtable on why startups fail, the founder’s dilemma, and the importance of understanding Letters of Intent.

💡 Honest conversations. Practical insights. Shared experiences.

And this is just the beginning.

iCreate’s CEO, Avinash Punekar, joined the 3rd National Space Day 2026 celebrations organised by ISRO - Indian Space Research Organization, for a panel discussion on “Scaling India’s New Space Ecosystem.”

Sharing an incubation and deep tech ecosystem perspective, he spoke about the critical role of incubators in helping emerging space enterprises move from innovation to scale, strengthening collaborations across the ecosystem and leveraging global partnerships to unlock new opportunities for India’s growing space economy.

The discussion brought together industry leaders, startups, investors and ecosystem enablers to explore the evolving role of private enterprises and collaboration in building a stronger and globally competitive Indian space ecosystem.

We are proud to celebrate NEMA AI, an iCreate-supported startup founded by Nidhi, for being named the Winner of the IIMA Healthcare Summit 2026, organised by Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad.

Competing through the Top 10 → Top 5 → Winner journey, NEMA AI showcased its innovative approach to enabling the early detection of cognitive decline and supporting timely intervention.

This recognition goes beyond a single startup milestone. Being recognised by one of India’s leading business schools is a strong validation of the scale and potential NEMA AI can achieve. It reflects the strength of the innovation and its ability to stand out on leading national platforms.

Congratulations to Nidhi and Team NEMA AI on this remarkable achievement! We are proud to see our startups taking their innovations to leading platforms and making their mark in India’s healthcare ecosystem.

Here’s to many more milestones ahead!
